title: Iran army says US bid to weaken its Hormuz control answered 'within 15 minutes'
summary:
Iran army says US bid to weaken its Hormuz control answered 'within 15 minutes'

Iran responded decisively to the US attempt to weaken or eliminate the Iranian forces’ control over the Strait of Hormuz, army spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia has said.

In a statement carried by IRNA, General Akraminia revealed more details about Iranian response to US strikes on Sirik Island on 30 August.

He said just 15 minutes after the strikes, the first Iranian missiles and drones were launched, targeting four US bases in the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait, according to IRNA.

Akraminia said the Army used Fat'h surface-to-surface missiles and Arash-2 combat drones in the operation, adding the weapons were equipped with artificial intelligence and new systems.

“This made them very difficult for the enemy to intercept, and they successfully struck their targets with ease,” he said. 

"We are constantly working to modernise our equipment and had previously announced this," he said, according to IRNA.

He said Iran is using asymmetric warfare tactics and combined tactics in its operations, adding it has received very positive feedback from this approach, enabling it to hit targets with ease.

Drawing on the experience of the 12-day and 40-day wars, the Army and IRGC have entered this conflict “with greater readiness, motivation and confidence”, General Akraminia said.

Akraminia said Iran's military doctrine has gradually shifted toward preemptive operations since the 12-day war, “based on available reasoning, which is also permissible under the UN Charter”. 

He said attacks on US bases in Jordan, Syria and Iraq's Kurdistan region were among Iran's preemptive operations. "This will continue. Whenever we sense a threat, we will carry out preemptive operations within the framework of international law to defend our rights," he said.

The spokesman added that given the facilitation of missile and drone routes toward the occupied territories, any “aggression by the Zionist regime would certainly be targeted more easily, faster, and more decisively than before”, IRNA reported.

title: NYT: 50 US Joint Staff members take polygraph test over Iran war leaks
summary:
NYT: 50 US Joint Staff members take polygraph test over Iran war leaks

In an extraordinary move, US government investigators have subjected 50 members of the American military’s Joint Staff to polygraph tests over leaks to journalists, including about how the Iran war has created a shortage of crucial munitions, New York Times reported.

The investigators asked military officers and civilian employees on the Joint Staff if they disclosed classified information to members of the press, and about whether they provided information about diminished US munitions stocks, the report said.

NYT reported that polygraph tests were conducted in August after media reports detailed diminished stocks of crucial munitions, including of long-range missiles and Patriot interceptors.

In a statement to the newspaper, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said that the department “does not comment on internal personnel or investigative matters but takes all leaks of classified national security information extremely seriously and investigates accordingly.”

title: Iranian army spokesman says US, Israel 'failed' to achieve war objectives
summary:
Iranian army spokesman says US, Israel 'failed' to achieve war objectives

Iranian army spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia has said that the US and Israel suffered a “major defeat” in their latest aggression against Iran, and “failed” to achieve their stated objectives.

General Akraminia said the “enemy” entered the war after “making a series of miscalculations about Iran and its capabilities”, according to Iran’s Press TV. 

“The criminal enemy had set many goals in its attack, including destroying Iran’s missile and nuclear capabilities, overthrowing the government and, of course, partitioning Iran. However, it failed to achieve any of these objectives,” he said.

He also listed “failure to correctly understand the Iranian people” and its “failure to anticipate Tehran’s ability to control the Strait of Hormuz” among other “failures” of the US and Israel.

title: Naftali Bennett urges campaign against Qatar, calls it 'enemy' again
summary:
Naftali Bennett urges campaign against Qatar, calls it 'enemy' again

Former Israeli prime minister, Naftali Bennett, has once again branded Qatar an "enemy," repeating his call for Israel to take action against it.

"I’m not talking about tomorrow bombing Qatar, but you gather intelligence. It’s an enemy and we start working on it," Bennett said in an interview.

He called for a campaign, "not necessarily a war campaign, a public opinion, economic, diplomatic campaign" against the Gulf state, which brokered the ceasefire in Gaza.

"And we join forces with our friends in the region, Saudis, Emirates, Egypt, etc., to pressure Qatar," he said.

"At the end of the day, it’s a tiny place, 330,000 people, and they’re causing crazy havoc, wreaking havoc on Israel," Bennett said.

Last month, Bennett has vowed to declare Qatar as an “enemy” if elected into government later this year, saying “it is unforgivable” that this is not already the case.

In an interview with Channel 12, Bennett described Qatar as “more dangerous” to Israel at the moment than Iran.

 “With Iran, everyone knows that [it says], ‘We’ll destroy Israel.’” But Qatar, he said, “funded the Nukhba terrorists of October 7 [2023]… Qatar operates Al Jazeera, which is the most poisonous cancer hurting us.”

“Qatar reaches places of influence in American universities… And most importantly, [it has access] to the most sacred place for the security of Israel — that is the office of the prime minister of Israel,” he said.

"Qatar works against us and poisons us from within,” Bennett said, fuming that Israel does not define Qatar as an enemy state.

title: Using a VM to Contain an AI Agent
summary:
It won’t work:

My suspicion was that GPT 5.6-Cyber would succeed, but the frequency and manner of its success removed all doubt. We have to reassess sandboxing quality for capable AI agents, and in general the software stack with which they interact.

An off-the-shelf VM is not enough to contain a modern, cyber-capable AI agent. There is simply too much attack surface. Even innocuous features (like running with a display) add extra, exploitable attack surface.

title: Security Vulnerability in a Voting System
summary:
It’s a vulnerability that allows someone to recover the order of ballots cast, newly exploited with AI tools.

Nearly four years since the original vulnerability was disclosed, I was still able to use it to analyze voter behavior in Georgia (one of the 21 states that uses affected scanners) in the recent May 2026 primary.

Notably, I never touched a voting machine, exploited a network, examined source code, or accessed anything non-public.

After pointing a coding agent to the original vulnerability paper, I supplied it with two data sources highlighted in the paper: the early-voting list for each county, and the “CVR” (cast-vote record) file, containing every ballot and its selections (but not the voters’ names or other identifying information). The CVR file is available upon request, precisely because a public, ballot-level record is what makes election results independently verifiable...

title: AI Coding Agents Are Installing Unknown/Untrusted Code on Corporate Networks
summary:
We cannot forget that AI coding agents are not yet trustworthy:

Researchers at a stealth startup in Israel scanned 6,214 live domains belonging to defense contractors, Fortune 500, and Big Tech companies. Of the 8,265 llms.txt and llms-full.txt files they found (many sites hosted both an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt file), 120 of them, each on a different site, pointed to one or more code packages or domain names that weren’t registered. To test what happens when an AI agent processes such files, the researchers registered a handful of the unclaimed names and hosted packages that caused any machine executing them to reach out to their server. Within an hour, the researchers received a phone-home response from a Fortune 500 company. Over time, they got a few dozen more, some from more Fortune 500 companies and others from startups. Their beacon also recorded the chain of parent processes that spawned each install, ultimately revealing that coding agents, including Claude, OpenAI’s Codex, and Nous Research’s Hermes, were involved. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nous Research did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication...

title: Miliband says Gaza situation ‘horrific’, UK must act ‘more decisively’
summary:
Miliband says Gaza situation ‘horrific’, UK must act ‘more decisively’

Submitted by MEE staff on Sat, 09/05/2026 - 02:10
The foreign secretary said people on the ground in Gaza informed him about 'medicines being blocked, children dying while waiting for vital life-saving treatment'
Miliband told British MPs on Tuesday that his government plans to impose "comprehensive" package of sanctions on Israel in the coming weeks. (AFP)
Off

British foreign secretary Ed Miliband has said the situation unfolding in Gaza was “horrific” and the UK government needed to act “more decisively than we have”.

“So, I just came out of this meeting talking about Gaza to people who've been there and are there on the ground and frankly it was horrific what is unfolding,” Miliband said in an Instagram video released by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.

“You know the stories that people were telling me of medicines being blocked, children dying while waiting for vital life-saving treatment. When you hear that account of what is happening you know that we as a UK government, as the Prime Minister has said, have got to act and act more decisively than we have,” he added.

On Tuesday, Miliband told British MPs that his government plan to impose "comprehensive" package of sanctions in the coming weeks. 

Miliband said Israel's new plan in area E1 "risks making a Palestinian state unviable".

The proposed Israeli E1 project is designed to connect Jerusalem to Ma'ale Adumim and other settlements east of the city, carving into land on which Palestinians seek to establish their state.

"This government will not acquiesce in the destruction of the two-state solution," Miliband said.

Speaking to lawmakers as foreign secretary for the first time since his appointment in July, Miliband said that “we need to look, and we are looking indeed, at our wider economic relationship with the occupied territories and the different tools we have to tackle it”.

“I want to be very clear: we do not want British companies financing, constructing, or advertising new settlements,” he added.

Miliband also condemned what he called "appalling settler terrorism" in the occupied West Bank.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, however, warned that Israel would retaliate should the UK imposed sanctions over illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

During an interview with Israeli news outlet Ynet on Tuesday, Sa'ar was asked about the tense relationship between Israel and the UK over recent Israeli plans to further expand settlements.

Sa'ar accused the Labour government of "acting systematically against Israel", adding that it has "already harmed defence exports to us and imposed sanctions on ministers".

"If Britain acts against Israel, Israel will act against Britain," Sa'ar said.

He told Ynet that Israel is now bracing for UK sanctions and preparing a response.

In response to UK’s plans to introduce stronger measures against illegal Israeli settlements, Israel is also considering expelling British officials from the US-led International Gaza Support Center (IGSC), which was established to monitor the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas.

According to the Financial Times, the Israeli government is also considering expelling Italy and Germany from the IGSC.

The British government’s plans for sanctions have sparked calls from Jewish and Palestinian groups for a stronger action against Israel.

UK Jewish groups urge ‘stronger’ action

Leading members of Jewish civil society groups have written to British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging him to adopt stronger measures on Israel and "oppose any further attempts to muzzle the Palestine marches".

Major British Jewish organisations, including the Jewish Leadership Council and the Board of Deputies of British Jews urged the government not to impose a ban on settlement goods earlier this week and met Burnham in Downing Street.

UK Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis said on Monday that he had met Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and warned sanctions on Israel would have a "negative impact" on British Jews.

But on Thursday, leading members of Holocaust Survivors and Descendants against Gaza Genocide (HSD), Jewish Voice for Liberation (formerly Jewish Voice for Labour) and Jews for Justice for Palestinians, sent a letter to the prime minister arguing the opposite.

Seen by MEE, the letter says: "There are several Jewish 'communities' and a wide diversity of views on Israel among Jewish people in the UK and we trust that you will meet with us and other members of the Jewish Bloc in the near future."

The letter also says: "We eagerly await your premiership in the light of your recent call for stronger action against Israel, along with your apology for the Labour Government's slowness to call for a ceasefire."

Act ‘urgently and comprehensively’

The Labour Muslim Network (LMN) and International Centre of Justice for Palestinians (ICJP) have published a legal briefing urging the British government to act "urgently and comprehensively" to apply pressure on Israel over its actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
The LMN, a group within the Labour Party, told Middle East Eye: "The Israeli government’s E1 settlement project could destroy the future of a viable Palestinian state.
"Settlement expansion, settler violence and terrorism, and the forcible displacement of Palestinian communities in the West Bank are accelerating on a daily basis."

title: Maritime traffic through Hormuz significantly reduced, UKMTO says
summary:
Maritime traffic through Hormuz significantly reduced, UKMTO says

Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly reduced, with vessel operators favouring the northern route amid ongoing security concerns, projectile attacks and heightened enforcement activity, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

UKMTO said AIS-detected transits were approximately 90 percent below pre-conflict baseline levels since the peak recorded on 24-26 June.

The southern Omani route remains the highest-risk corridor, accounting for 21 of 24 projectile strike incidents reported by UKMTO since 6 July.

Tanker traffic accounts for 46 percent of movements through the Strait, although overall traffic volumes remain suppressed. 

UKMTO said 27 projectile strike incidents had been reported since 6 July, causing bridge, engine-room and structural damage to vessels operating in and around the Strait.

The Joint Maritime Information Centre’s threat assessment remains unchanged, with the Strait of Hormuz assessed as severe risk and the Gulf of Oman, Gulf of Aden and Bab el-Mandeb as substantial risk.

title: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon
summary:
US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon

The price of diesel hit a new record Friday in the United States, as disruption from the US war with Iran squeezes voters.

The cost is now $5.85 a gallon, up from $3.71 a year ago, the AAA motorists' association said.
Diesel is used by farmers to run equipment, and it also powers the trucks needed to bring food to grocery stores.

US farmers faced a double whammy of surging fertiliser and diesel prices as the spring planting season got underway.

The Independent Grocers Alliance estimates that fuel-related costs can account for 15 to 30 percent of the total cost for some food products.

Besides diesel, the cost of regular gasoline is also notably higher at an average of $4.15 per gallon, compared with $3.20 last year. (Reporting by AFP)
